stops.note: a napkin or cloth; the magistrate presiding at the Circus started the chariot races by dropping a white mappa (the same word later gave 'map')
a small cloth, diminutive of nape 'tablecloth', from mappa; related to English 'napkin'
Middle English napron, a cloth worn in front; 'a napron' was heard as 'an apron', and by the 1500s the n had gone

current_meaning: a protective garment worn over the front of one's clothes
